content.text:
Demo 2's output looks strange—it seems to delete everything except a fragment, as if the selector picks out only the occluded shapes and places them on a blank canvas at their minimal row/col position. In demo 1, the occluded shape happened to be the complete diagonal, but in demo 2, the diagonal is split, so maybe only a shorter occluded segment gets recognized and output.

So the actual rule seems to be: output only the occluded shape(s) on a blank canvas, and demo 2's example is just messy since the rectangle splits the diagonal into disconnected pieces. I think I should avoid that ambiguity and instead build clearer demos like the original—one diagonal fully crossing the grid, occluded by a rectangle, so the full diagonal is restored as output. I'll add two more such demos to reinforce this pattern, including one with a 12x12 anti-diagonal occluded by a rectangle spanning several rows and columns.
